header.running_head: Enemies Lose their Sight by the Curses of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA)

blocks.arabic_text: عَلَيْهِمْ ۗ وَكَانَ اللّٰهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُوْنَ بَصِيْرًا
blocks.text: It is Allaah Who restrained their hands from (fighting) you and your hands from (fighting) them right in Makkah (at Hudaybiyyah) after granting you dominance over them. Allaah is always Watchful over what you do.
A Man Loses his Sight by the Curse of Hadhrat Ali (RA)

Hadhrat Zaadhaan narrates that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) once narrated a Hadith, someone accused him of lying. "May I curse you if it is you who are lying?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked the man. "Go ahead and curse," the man challenged. The man had not even left the gathering when his eyesight was lost.[^2]

Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) once narrated a Hadith, someone accused him of lying. The man had hardly stood up from the gathering and he was already blind (because of the curse of Hadhrat Ali (RA)).[^3]

Hadhrat Zaadhaan narrates that when someone once narrated a Hadith to Hadhrat Ali (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I think that you are lying to me." When the man insisted that he was not, Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked, "May I curse you if you are lying?" "Go ahead and curse," the man challenged. Hadhrat Ali (RA) then cursed the man and he had scarcely left the gathering when he became blind.[^4]
A Woman becomes Blind by the Curse of Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid (RA)

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Marwaan once sent some people to Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid (RA) to discuss a claim that a woman named Arwa bint Uwais had made against him. Hadhrat Sa'eed (RA) exclaimed, "These people think that I have wronged her when I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'The one who usurps even a hand's span of land, will have a hand's span of all seven earths placed as a yoke around his neck on the Day of Qiyaamah.'" Hadhrat Sa'eed (RA) then prayed, "O Allaah! If she is lying, let her not die until she turns blind and make her well her grave."
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "By Allaah! She turned blind before her death and one day as she very cautiously left her house, she fell into her well and it became her grave."[^5]

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazam
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazam narrates that a woman named Arwa once sought judgement from Marwaan bin Hakam against Hadhrat
Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.145). Nasa'ee has reported a similar narration, as quoted in the Tafseer of Ibn Katheer (Vol.4 Pg.192).
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.116) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Ibn Abi Dunya, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.8 Pg.5).
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.96).
